extracted.intended_audience: Scientists (early-career) applying for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (URF) or Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship (DHF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing applications to the Royal Society University Research Fellowship and Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship schemes, focusing on assessment criteria, what makes a strong research proposal, the applicant's track record, and choice of UK Host Organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed using three broad criteria: The scientific track record of the applicant; The strength of the scientific proposal; The suitability of the proposed UK Host Organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three dimensions are the high-level axes the Panel uses to judge applications; applicants should ensure their materials address all three.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate timing to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply 'when you have formulated a vision for how your independent research program will develop over the next 5-10 years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: URFs and DHFs are for scientists ready to become independent researchers; you should know which scientific questions to address and how you want your independent programme to develop. The plan should be distinct from your previous supervisors' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific track record — publications from PhD and subsequent positions
rubrics_metrics.description: You should have published research from both your PhD and any subsequent research positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It can be beneficial to have publications not all within a very narrow field. If publishing independent papers is uncommon in your field, describe leadership roles in producing papers in the career summary. You may include preprints in your publications list. The Royal Society follows DORA: publications are reviewed on scientific content, not journal metrics or identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain contributions to key papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly explain your contributions to key papers on your personal statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially important for papers with supervisors or large collaborations — clarify your role and leadership where applicable so panels understand your independence and specific contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated engagement and leadership activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional activities such as organising conferences, public communication of science, and collaborative projects are valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities show energy and enthusiasm and can strengthen the application, but should not come at the expense of a solid scientific track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research vision and independent programme
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a fellowship proposal: present a research vision and a feasible approach for an independent research programme (5–10 year outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are funding the person as well as the project. Show how your programme is independent of previous supervisors and outline long-term development, not just a single project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big research questions and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear signposting of your big research questions and why the problem is important and interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the impact of expected outcomes on your field and career. Sections describing importance should be comprehensible to scientists in similar areas (e.g., a theoretical physicist should understand a computer science proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach and methods — feasibility and technical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how you will address the problem and present the methods you will use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological section (c) should be more technical to convince specialised reviewers you know what you're doing. Demonstrate a feasible approach while allowing for ambitious elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: State what you expect the outcome to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline anticipated results and how they advance the field and your research trajectory; this helps panels judge feasibility and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity for mixed reviewer expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Write sections so that parts are accessible to general reviewers and other parts are technical for experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections on importance and broad aims (a and d, and probably b) should be comprehensible to scientists in similar areas; the methods (c) should be technical for specialist referees. Get feedback from both within and outside your field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit between applicant and proposed research (person-as-investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate why you are the right person to answer your research questions; show research productivity across career stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track record suggests you'll manage obstacles; emphasize skills, previous achievements, leadership, and how your background positions you to deliver the proposed programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition and risk profile — allow some high-risk, high-gain work
rubrics_metrics.description: Include elements that are not entirely 'safe' — some high-risk, high-gain signalling ambitious and innovative thinking is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance feasibility with ambition; show how risks will be managed and justify the potential payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations — include those that expand and train
rubrics_metrics.description: Include scientific collaborations that expand and improve your research and contribute to training for you and your group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight how collaborations will add knowledge/training and how your expertise will benefit collaborators. Explain contributions to large collaborations and leadership roles (e.g., leading working groups) and how your proposed work goes beyond collaboration's normal plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek advice from diverse colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Get feedback from senior colleagues, field experts, and colleagues in different scientific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the proposal will be read by both expert referees and general reviewers, obtain input from people within and outside your field to ensure clarity and robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Organisation — collaborative links, facilities, training, and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a Host Organisation that provides collaborative links, access to facilities, and training and development options that enhance your research; the host should support you from application to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many hosts provide mentorship during preparation; detail how the host will support the fellowship with space, resources, and mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host prospects for growth and permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider prospects for a permanent position after the fellowship and opportunities to grow your research group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate opportunities for collaboration within the department, space and resources for group growth, and longer-term career prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staying at current Host Organisation — show independence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is acceptable to stay at your current host organisation, but you must show how you will gain independence and how your research will be distinct from previous supervisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how you will be positioned as an independent researcher (e.g., distinguish topics so you and your former supervisor could speak in the same session on related but different topics in five years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a UK Host when applying from outside the UK
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a Host Organisation that will help you prepare the application and support the fellowship with space, resources, and possibly longer-term prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for active places in your field that provide feedback on proposals, practice interviews, and clear commitments regarding support during the fellowship.
